semantics.disposition: Current migration ownership, not a claim of implemented parity. Transitional TypeScript remains until the named target passes differential fixtures.
semantics.zero_behavior_change: Only additive declarations and unavailable adapters. No runtime provider, facade, transform, historian, config loader, database open or migration is redirected.
semantics.host_inputs: Each key names a dependency the engine does not fully produce today. current_source names the producer, mostly TypeScript; a Rust path may identify a partial consumer or authenticated binding. target names final producer ownership, including policy producers that must move into core.
semantics.new_capabilities: C03, C04 and C11 are proposed new work, not existing TypeScript parity.
semantics.config_boundary: ConfigNamespaces.core() returns CoreConfig only; bridge settings have a distinct BridgeConfig type. Existing McModuleConfig loading remains unchanged.
semantics.registration: Each listed namespace mod.rs is compiled at wave 0A. In wave 1 its sole editor is the slice whose owned_files lists it: 1A context_schema/mod.rs, 1C config_parity/mod.rs, 1D retrieval/mod.rs. Each adds mod lines for its implementation files; no wave-1 worker edits crates/mc-module/src/lib.rs or crates/mc-store/src/lib.rs. After wave 1 retrieval/mod.rs belongs only to the serial integrator, never concurrent 2D/3A-3C slices; context_schema/mod.rs passes serially from 1A to 2A. No build script or Cargo changes.
semantics.authority: RequestContext.route is a non-deserializable transport binding; constructors do not authenticate. Bridges must validate native facts, and implementations must compare embedded archive scopes with the authenticated route before writes. Ordinals are inclusive and carry explicit zero/one bases. Version/generation/hash/model fencing is an implementation obligation, not implemented by these DTOs.
